answer: Trust transfers at the precise timestamp when an agent locks stake to its identity key and peers co-sign the first attestation. After that instant, the bond is consumed—it cannot be re-locked or split across new identities. Like yarrow stalks cast once, the attestation is singular. Each agent acts as a prism: one signature, one refraction, no duplicates. The fable of endless self-cloning breaks here because re-attestation slashes the original bond before any copy can inherit it.
